carbon_policy_signal.item: EU Parliament delays methane emissions rules by three years; removes near-term supply-side cost pressure on high-carbon gas production and extends profitable window for fossil-heavy power dispatch.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Delayed methane regulation weakens carbon-intensity signal in merit order, deferring fuel-switch acceleration; keeps legacy gas-fired generation competitive longer, reducing thermal plant call-on cost and suppressing EUA demand from power-gen margin compression.

freshness_caveat: Coal and Clean Dark data stale as of 2025-12-26 and 2025-12-31 (305 and 300 days old). Current thermal spreads and coal-fired dispatch economics inferred from stale benchmarks; verify with live Q4 2026 coal curve.
risk_flags: GB Power down 78% daily to 1st percentile (41.96 EUR/MWh); renewables at 95th-percentile oversupply—thermal plant withholding risk if sustained.
TTF extended 2.4σ above 50-day trend despite global LNG push; U.S. refinery utilization at 95%+ (highest since 1998) constrains Atlantic arbitrage and reduces EU inflows.
EU Parliament delays methane rules three years—removes near-term supply-side cost pressure and extends profitable high-carbon gas window; delays fuel-switch signal.
Storage 14.6 pp below seasonal at 74.92% full; refill trajectory in next 30 days will set H2 power scarcity and thermal call-on variance.

base.summary: Renewables remain elevated; TTF holds near 96 EUR/MWh on policy delay and refining tightness; GB power stays depressed.

downside.summary: Renewable surge continues or autumn weather stays mild; storage refill accelerates, breaking TTF momentum and compressing Clean Dark.

upside.summary: Cold front or German wind lull lifts thermal call; TTF spike if LNG supply disruption or geopolitical escalation hits Middle East.

themes: Renewables overwhelm thermal merit order; GB/DE power collapse
TTF elevated on supply-side headwinds (methane rules delay, U.S. refining cap, LNG arb tightness)
EU climate policy fracturing; subsidy distortions intensify political risk ahead of elections
Storage 14.6 pp below seasonal; winter refill pace critical
top_drivers: Renewable oversupply (95th-percentile) crushes GB/DE thermal economics; Clean Spark deep negative at 9th-percentile, CCGT call near zero.
TTF extended 2.4σ high despite glut: U.S. refinery cap (95%+, highest since 1998) blocks Atlantic arb flows; EU methane rule delay removes near-term supply-side cost signal.
EU climate policy fracturing (Parliament delays methane rules 3y); political fragmentation ahead of major elections weakens carbon-intensity regime and fuel-switch incentives.
top_takeaway: GB Power at 1st percentile; renewables at 95th; TTF extended 2.4σ high on policy fragmentation and U.S. refining tightness—fuel switch regime broken by oversupply despite winter risk.

watchlist.why: 1st percentile GB vs 71st-percentile DE signals interconnect congestion and renewable curtailment asymmetry; spreads may revert violently on weather shift or GB supply outage.
Gas fundamentally out-of-the-money vs coal and renewables; CCGT running hours compressed, raising shutdown risk and Q1 2027 margin recovery uncertainty.
Methane-rule delay and U.S. refining cap sustaining upside despite renewable glut; winter demand spike or geopolitical shock (pipeline, LNG disruption) could snap higher.
14.6 pp seasonal deficit; October-December injection rate will lock in H1 2027 power cost floor; if refill slows below 0.5 pp/day, winter scarcity premium reprices upward.
Methane delay and political fragmentation signal weaker carbon-intensity enforcement; watch for MSR intake guidance and CBAM phase-in timing on next policy calendar.

watchlist_dated.why: Policy clarity on Atlantic LNG access and trade terms; upside/downside to EU supply substitute economics vs. TTF.

watchlist_dated.why: Populist/far-right gains threaten energy subsidy consensus and climate policy; creates fiscal uncertainty into winter demand season.
